aiActionDescription.fixGrammar: Corrects spelling, grammar, and punctuation without changing the meaning.
aiActionDescription.improveClarity: Makes the text clearer and easier to read while keeping all content unchanged.
aiActionDescription.makeShorter: Shortens the text while keeping all essential concepts and information.

aiDesc08b: The lightest option. Runs on modest hardware; ideal for quick grammar corrections, though not always precise.
aiDesc27b: Workstation-grade. Requires considerable disk space and memory; ideal for greater precision in suggestions.
aiDesc2b: Small and fast, with better grammar than 0.8B.
aiDesc4b: The best balance between quality and resource requirements.
aiDesc9b: Superior quality; requires a capable machine.
aiDescription: Disabled. It is not uninstalled from the device, though.

aiError.badSelection: This selection cannot be rewritten. It may be empty or longer than a single passage.
aiError.daemon: Ollama could not complete the operation.
aiError.disabled: The AI assistant is disabled. You can enable it in the settings.
aiError.empty: The model did not return anything. Try again, making sure a model is selected.
aiError.modelGone: That model is no longer installed. Choose another one in the settings.
aiError.noModel: You have not chosen a model yet. Select one on the settings page.
aiError.noPassage: The model did not return a rewritten passage.
aiError.reasoned: The model received the request but did not return any text. A shorter passage is usually enough to resolve this error.
aiError.timeout: The model took too long and was stopped. A shorter passage is usually enough to resolve this error.
aiError.tooLong: The model was stopped because the content may be too long. Nothing was changed.
aiError.unreachable: Ollama is not responding. Make sure it is running on your computer before trying again.
aiError.unreadable: The model's response does not appear to be readable.

aiHint: AI models run locally on your computer through Ollama. No data is ever sent outside your device. Privacy is one of Wattle's founding principles and what sets it apart: your data always stays on your computer.
aiMayNotFit: At the limit for this computer
aiMayNotFitHint: This model requires more memory than this machine has available. It may be slow or fail to start altogether. Installation can still be performed even though it is not recommended.
aiModelsDescription: Installed and available models. Nothing is downloaded until you ask for it.
aiNoModelChosenHint: The AI assistant is active, but no model is active yet. Choose one above to start using AI features.
aiNoModelsYet: No model is installed yet. Choose one below: nothing is downloaded until you ask for it.
aiOnDescription: A model running on this device. Nothing is sent elsewhere, to respect your privacy.
aiPreparing: Getting the assistant ready on this computer…
aiRecommendedHint: Best match for this computer's memory.
aiRemoveConfirm: {{name}} will be deleted from this computer. Do you want to continue?
aiSectionDescription: Optional, local, and off until you turn it on.
aiUnmanagedDescription: Installed outside Wattle. You can remove it from here, but it is not offered as an active model.
allSparksIntro: Every spark you have captured, shown from the most recent. They are intentionally short and untitled: a spark is a note for yourself, a thought caught in the moment, with no rules except your own.
backupDescription: Save a copy of your pages, attachments, and settings.
backupFolderHint: This is where backup .wattle files are written, with the day's file name. It is not where your journal is kept. Previous backups are never included in a new one.
backupFolderUnset: Not set yet: the save dialog starts wherever Windows last left it.
backupHint: Wattle asks where to save the file each time. Database, attachments, and settings in a single .wattle file. Ollama models are not included and can be easily installed directly from Wattle.
calendarIntro: Where your writing falls throughout the year. A fuller day is a day when you wrote more; select one to read it again.

components.cardBody: A simple surface: thin border, card background, nothing else.
components.dialogBody: A dialog in a portal, with the background and close button provided by this project.
components.pageDescription: One or two sentences about what the screen is for, below the way back, the title, and what the screen puts on the right.
components.popoverBody: Anchored to its trigger and closed by anything else: this is where both the date field and a letter's deadline open.
components.sampleEntryBody: Left early enough to walk there, and the fog was still hanging over the field behind the houses.
components.sampleEntryOpening: Left early enough to walk there, and the
components.sampleEntryTitle: The long way to the station
components.sampleSpark: Whatever it is, it is not urgent. Sleep on it.
components.subtitle: The pieces that make up the interface, with their variants and states. Primitives first; then the few functional components used across enough screens to be worth seeing on their own. Everything here uses mock data.
components.title: Components
components.tooltipBody: An explanation, one step behind the control it belongs to.
components.tourBody: The page darkens, the highlighted element stays lit, and the card follows it. Every guided tour in Wattle is this, one step at a time.

dataSectionDescription: Your journal, in and out of Wattle.
deleteEntryConfirm: This page moves to the trash. You can restore it from Settings until it is removed for good.
deleteSparkConfirm: This spark moves to the trash. You can restore it from Settings until it is removed for good.
editorScaleDescription: How large your writing is set in the editor.
editorScaleHint: Only the writing changes size - the rest of the application stays as it is.
emptyBody: Every page stays on this device. Start today, even with a single line.
emptySparksBody: A spark is a line caught in the moment. The field above is where one starts.
emptyTitle: Your journal starts with a page.
entryContentPlaceholder: Write something, or press / for commands…
entryLockDescription: A page that already contains something opens locked. One click is all it takes to unlock it.
entryLockHint: A new page starts empty and will never be locked until you finish it. This option only applies to journal pages that already exist.
exportDescription: The entire journal as an HTML archive that opens without a network connection.
exportEmpty: There is nothing to export yet: the journal has no pages in it.
exportError: Export failed. Your journal was not changed.
journalFolderConfirm: Choose a folder and Wattle will move your journal into it - the database and every attachment together. Wattle reopens once the move is done. If it cannot be moved, your journal stays exactly where it is.
journalFolderError: The journal could not be moved. It is still where it was, and nothing was changed.
journalFolderHint: This is where the journal itself is kept: wattle.db and your attachments. It is not where backup .wattle files are saved.
languageHint: Only changes the interface. It does not touch a word of what you have written.
layoutWidthDescription: How wide all of Wattle's pages are.
layoutWidthHint: Set the width of Wattle's pages yourself. Every computer and every monitor can be different, so we leave the ideal value up to you.
letterArrivedTitle: A letter from your past self has arrived
letterComposeDescription: Something you will not be able to read until a day you choose. Once sealed, it cannot be opened, edited, or deleted. Choose carefully.
letterContentPlaceholder: Choose what to write before sealing your letter.
letterDraftRow_one: A letter started - {{count}} word so far
letterDraftRow_other: A letter started - {{count}} words so far

letterError.badDate: That is not a date for which this letter can be sealed.
letterError.corrupt: This letter cannot be opened. Its seal no longer matches how it was closed: this happens when the opening date, encrypted text, or key is modified in the journal file after sealing.
letterError.empty: There is nothing written to seal yet.
letterError.futureEnvelope: This letter was sealed by a newer version of Wattle. Update Wattle to open it.
letterError.noKey: This letter's key is gone. The only way forward is to restore a backup made before it disappeared.
letterError.notYet: This letter has not opened yet. Come back later.
letterError.sealed: This letter is sealed and it is not time to open it yet. Come back later.
letterError.tooFar: A letter can wait at most fifty years.
letterError.tooSoon: A letter must wait at least seven days.

letterReviewBody: Read it one last time. After this step, it is put away.
letterSealBody: It will be encrypted and put away until {{date}}.
letterSealFailed: The letter was not sealed. Nothing was changed.
letterSealHonesty: Wattle encrypts the letter and keeps the key in the journal file, so the letter cannot be lost. It is a lock against yourself, not a secret from whoever has access to your computer - and a backup carries both halves with it.
letterSealTerms: Until {{date}}, you will not be able to open, read, edit, delete, or change its date. Neither will Wattle. The only way to remove it is to clear the entire journal.
letterWaitingLine: A letter to yourself opens on {{date}}.
lettersDescription: Words you entrust to your future self. Choose a day and leave there whatever you want to remember, tell, or rediscover. Until then, the letter stays sealed and out of reach.
lettersEmptyBody: A letter is something you write now and cannot read again until a day you choose.
listErrorBody: Your pages are still on this device: Wattle could not read them. Try again and, if the problem persists, restore a backup.
memoriesSectionDescription: Two ways for what you have written to come back to you.
memoryAsk: Find a memory worth reading again
memoryNoneAlike: Nothing else you have written is similar enough to this to be worth placing beside it.
memoryNoneLeft: Nothing else is similar enough to be worth showing.
memoryTooRecent: There is nothing far enough back yet. A memory must be at least two weeks older than your most recent writing, and your journal does not go back far enough yet.
name: Name
nameHint: Choose how you want to be called in Wattle, with your real name or an invented one. You can change it whenever you want.
nameRequired: Name is required: at least {{min}} characters.
navigationDescription: Where the main navigation is located.
navigationHint: Place the navigation wherever you prefer it.
newProfileConfirmBody: Every page, every attachment, and your name will be permanently deleted and the setup will start over. This action cannot be undone.
newProfileDescription: Sign out, delete this profile, and start from scratch. Every page and every attachment will be deleted. You can still back up this profile before confirming.
newProfileError: Unable to start over. Your journal was not changed.
newProfileHint: There is only one journal on this device. This action clears it; it does not add a second one.
newProfileNoBackupBody: Wattle has no record of a backup for this journal. Everything it contains is about to be deleted and, without a backup, there is no way to recover it.
ollamaInstallFailed: Ollama could not be installed. Wattle did not change anything on this device.
ollamaStartFailed: Ollama did not start in time. It may still be starting up: try again in a moment.
onThisDayDescription: The pages you wrote in previous years, on today's date, will appear on the home page.
onThisDayHint: Choose whether you want to see again what you wrote on this same date in previous years. The reminder appears on the home page.

start.title: Have you kept a journal with Wattle before?
start.body: If you have a backup, everything in it will return to its place.
start.freshBody: A blank first page, and three short questions before you open it.
start.returningBody: Texts, attachments, and settings, exactly as you left them.

returning.title: Let's find your journal.
returning.body: Choose the .wattle backup file you saved. Everything it contains replaces this empty journal, and Wattle opens where you left off.
returning.confirm: Choose the .wattle file you saved and Wattle will reopen with everything it contains: texts, attachments, and settings. This empty journal will be replaced.

name.title: What should Wattle call you?
name.body: Used for the greeting on the home screen. Two to twelve characters.

backup.title: Where should backups be saved?
backup.body: A folder outside the journal, so a backup is somewhere else when you need it.

theme.title: Light or dark?
theme.body: You can change it whenever you want in the settings.

paletteDescription: Sets the colors, typefaces, and visual style of Wattle.
paletteHint: Changes the look of the whole app: background, text, interface details, corners, and typefaces. It does not change anything you have written.
replayToursDescription: Show all welcome tours again. Useful for rediscovering all of Wattle's features.
replayToursHint: Marks all tours as unseen and takes you to the home screen to show you the first one.
resetConfirm: Appearance, page width, memories, and page locking return to their initial settings. The journal, your name, and AI assistant settings are not touched. Do you want to continue?
resetDescription: Return to the initial values. Your name and AI assistant settings remain as they are.
resetHint: Preferences only. Pages, sparks, and letters remain exactly where they are.
restoreConfirm: Every page, attachment, and setting on this device will be replaced by the backup you choose now. This action cannot be undone.
restoreDescription: Replaces everything on this device with a backup.
restoreError: Restore failed. Your data was not touched.
restoreHint: Replaces everything on this device with the backup. This cannot be undone.
searchDisabledHint: No items found; add an item before you can enable search.
searchSparksDisabledHint: There is nothing to search yet: write a spark above and search will become active.
settingsSubtitle: Everything you find here is saved on this device.

taskList.description: Keep track of things to do
taskList.title: Checklist

sparkDate: Day this spark is archived under
sparkEchoDescription: An earlier spark returns on its own, at most one per day.
sparkEchoHint: A spark at least 30 days old, the same one for the whole day, then the next one tomorrow.
sparkRichBody: This spark contains formatting or attachments, from before sparks became plain text. Nothing has been changed: it opens in the full editor, where everything continues to work.
sparkTruncated_one: The most recent one is shown.
sparksIntro: A line or two, caught before they get away. Nothing here needs a title, and nothing needs to become something else.
themeDescription: Every theme exists in both; this is the one you are reading in.
themeHint: The theme applies to the whole app, and your choice is remembered the next time you open it.

switch.title: Off until you turn it on
switch.body: The AI assistant is optional and starts off. It improves and personalises the experience inside Wattle, always with respect for your privacy. The data is processed on your computer and will never leave it.

runtime.title: What the models run on
runtime.body: The models run through Ollama. Wattle can install it and start it from here, if you let it.

models.title: The models you keep
models.body: Download the model best suited to your computer. Try one at a time, so you can tell which one fits your hardware best.

write.title: Start with today
write.body: This is how a new page begins. One click opens a blank page with today's date: even a single line deserves a place here.

search.title: Find what you wrote
search.body: Every word on every page is searchable, and the result shows the matching passage. It stays disabled until there is something to search.

timeline.title: Everything you have written
timeline.body: Your pages, from the most recent and grouped by month. Open one to continue, or scroll to load more.

nav.title: Everything else
nav.body: The calendar, sparks, letters to yourself, and settings all live in this bar. It follows you from screen to screen, and the one you are on is the only one that carries its own name.

grid.title: Your journal by date
grid.body: The days you wrote are marked. Choose one to read it again, or to write on a day that has already passed.

view.title: A month, or a whole year
view.body: Switch between the two. It is in the yearly view that a habit becomes visible.

kinds.title: pages, sparks, or both
kinds.body: Two types of writing share this grid, distinguished by the color of their marks. Show one at a time when you are looking for something specific.

capture.title: Capture a thought
capture.body: A spark is a line caught in the moment. No title, no page. Write it and press Ctrl+Enter, or use the button.

archive.title: All the sparks you have kept
archive.body: Here you will find the latest ones. From here you can open them all, month by month - and write a new one from there too.

recent.title: What a spark can become
recent.body: Each one opens on its own page, where you can edit it, delete it, or turn it into a proper page if it has grown in the meantime.

title.title: Give it a name, or leave it as it is
title.body: The title is optional and saves automatically as you write. Press Enter to move directly to the page below.

editor.title: Type "/" for everything else
editor.body: Write here as you would on paper. Typing "/" opens the pop-up menu with everything the page can contain: headings, lists, quotes, images, videos, and files. Select text to format it. There is nothing to save: it is written as you go.

actions.title: Page commands
actions.body: Go to the previous or next page, lock it against accidental edits, export it as HTML, or delete it.

appearance.title: Make it yours
appearance.body: Theme, accent color, language, and page width.

data.title: Your journal is yours
data.body: Back it up, export it as HTML, or restore it from a backup. Everything stays on this device.

reset.title: Go back
reset.body: Return preferences to their original state, replay these tours, or start a completely new journal.

profile.title: Your name, and nothing else
profile.body: It greets you on the home screen and never leaves this device. Wattle asks nothing else of you: no account, no email, no sign-in.

what.title: A letter to yourself
what.body: It is not a page: a letter is written now and remains sealed until a day you choose. Until then it cannot be read, edited, or unsealed - not even by you.

write.title: Write one
write.body: One draft at a time, kept here until you seal it. Sealing asks for the day it will open, and there is no going back.

waiting.title: While it waits
waiting.body: A sealed letter shows only the day it opens and how long it is. No countdown, no preview: it will simply be here when the time comes.

directions.title: Where to start
directions.body: Choose a direction and you will be given a question to write toward. The question is not saved and never becomes part of the letter: it is simply something to look at while you write.

seal.title: When it will open
seal.body: Choose how far away that day is, then read it one last time. Sealing is final: from that moment, the letter is unreadable until the chosen date.

opened.title: It has arrived
opened.body: The day you chose has arrived and the letter can be read!

keep.title: Yours, forever
keep.body: Read it as many times as you want. It cannot be edited once sealed, and it cannot be deleted.

trashDescription: Pages you delete wait here before they are gone for good.
trashEmptyConfirm: Every page waiting in the trash will be permanently deleted, attachments included. This action cannot be undone.
trashError: The trash could not be read.
trashHint: A restored page comes back with its date, its attachments and its place in the journal.
trashIntro: A deleted page waits here for {{days}} days, and is then removed for good.
trashPurgeConfirm: This page and everything attached to it will be permanently deleted. This action cannot be undone.
writingSectionDescription: How a page behaves when you open it.
letterAiUnavailableBody: The directions above always work. To also get a question to start from, turn on the AI assistant and choose a model in Settings - it runs on this computer, and nothing leaves it.
